chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan.

He said: "Thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and two rakʿahs before Salat al-Fajr. That is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to pray, and if there had been any additional virtue, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله would have acted upon it more and had the greatest right to it."

key_terms.أَعْمَلَ بِهِ: more active in performing it, indicating stronger adherence
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act being asked about in Ramadan
key_terms.الْوَتْرُ: the Witr prayer, included within the total count
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: thirteen rakʿahs, the total number mentioned
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose practice is the proof
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the time context of the ruling
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the Fajr prayer, before which two rakʿahs are prayed

ai.seo_question: How many rakʿahs of recommended salat are prayed in Ramadan according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed number of recommended night prayers in the month of Ramadan as thirteen rakʿahs, including al-Witr and two rakʿahs before Fajr. It grounds the ruling in the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, indicating that no additional increase is more virtuous than what he consistently performed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1564 - Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the prayer during the month of Ramadan.

Imam (as) said: "Thirteen rak'ahs, including the Witr prayer and two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer. This is how the Messenger of Allah (sw) used to pray, and if there was any greater virtue in adding more, the Messenger of Allah (sw) would have been the most diligent and deserving of it."
